title: His outlook and featuring his sidemen
summary: He featured Dud and others and says he has nothing to regret.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Looking back: no regrets, what it all meant

blocks.x: You know, as I sit and talk with you, and get the information, you know, from all of the different sides, I mean, that which you remember and that which you relate to is a great part of your success must have been your ability to take a nice approach to what's going on around you and to be able to utilize all the things that happened and make a profitable package out of that. I mean, I'm saying, in addition to your talent as a trumpet player or as a band leader, I mean, you just seem to have a particular type of personality that draws people toward you, and that seems to make them realize that there is strength (inaudible) there, and you
can sort of hold them together and make some- thing that wouldn't exist without your presence.
Now, it's very unusual to hear you say anything about not liking a particular person. (Inaudible).

I have been that way all my life as far as I can remember back. If I believe in a person, I think if he has some- thing there he should have just as much chance as I have if I can do it, like all the fellows in my band.

Like, when I got to New York, certain people said that I should be taking this solo. I should do it, I was bringing in Dud Bascomb and the other trumpet players in the band. I said no, let them take one too. Let them play. If they can play a solo, whoever it is, let them feature.

If you've noticed, a lot of my records, I featured Bobby Johnson, after Dud, and all the rest of the names on there. They played too. But, if I, I just can't take nothing from nobody. If I know he's got that ability,
they've got to be there. And, I just feel good for people. As long as a person is a person and he feels good and he can do this, if I can help, more power to him.
That outlook seems to have paid off for you.
I've had nothing to regret that I can remember.

That's what I meant. That's one of the big things, the way that it pays off for you. You have nothing to regret, and you feel good, you know, about what you've done and what other people have done, and your career, and you're still in the middle of it. I mean, you're projecting into the future. You're seeing things from here. I mean, you're not, you're comfortable as you say. I mean, but, you are not driven by any particular thing to do. But, you're just there, and sort of in the middle and directing it from all sides, which must be a good feeling.
It is. It made me feel good. Here, I just do practically what I

feel like doing. And what I don't feel like doing, I won't do it. But, I won't do nothing to hurt nobody. You know, I like to cooperate with people. I'll give. It's like if they give, I'll give too. But, I won't, if I find out that people don't want to be bothered, I won't push myself on them, you know.
